The best free IPTV player with no ads

November 27, 2026

"Free" means different things in IPTV players. Some are free with ads. Some are free for a week, then ask for a licence per device. A few are free with no ads at all. Here's how the popular players line up, from what each developer says on its own pages.

One thing first: a player is only the app. The channels come from your provider, and no player, Tuned included, comes with any. Be wary of any "free IPTV" that offers channels too; see is IPTV legal?

Free, ads or trial: how the players compare

PlayerFree to use?Ads

"Not stated" means we couldn't find it on the developer's own pages. Prices and ads change, so check before you rely on it. Each link has the full comparison and its sources.

What you get free in Tuned

Tuned is free on Android phones, tablets, Android TV and Google TV, with no ads and no trial clock. The free app isn't a demo:

  • One playlist: an Xtream Codes login, an M3U link or file, a MAC portal, or a Plex, Jellyfin or Emby server, with its TV guide.
  • Live TV, films and shows, with search, favourites and Continue Watching.
  • The whole player: captions and subtitle search, sound tracks, picture-in-picture and casting to your TV.
  • The grid guide, channel numbers and the last-channel button.
  • Backup copies of channels that stop working, and the Live events page.
  • Up to three downloads at a time for offline viewing.

What Premium adds, if you want it

Nothing nags you to upgrade. A locked feature shows a lock, and that's all. Premium adds more than one playlist, profiles with kids profiles and PINs, your own lists, pause and rewind on live TV, recording, following events, more than three downloads at once, Trakt and Simkl, and a Tuned account that backs everything up. It's US$9.99 a year with a 7-day free trial, or US$24.99 once, for up to three devices.

Why "free with ads" costs more than it looks

Ads in a video player aren't only annoying. They load from the internet while you watch, and on a busy TV box that can mean slower menus or a stutter in the stream. A player with no ads has nothing competing with your channel for the connection.

Tuned goes further: it only ever uses one stream connection. No live previews, no background downloads while you watch, so you stay inside your provider's limit. More in how many devices can I use IPTV on?
